result.topic_en: Euler states Problem I, finding the differential variation of the integral of Z dx where Z depends on x, y and the successive derivatives p, q, r, s, and derives it by integration by parts into an integral part and boundary terms.
result.transcription:
116 DE METHODO
in variatum transfertur, accipit, definiatur; quippe
quod nihilo aequale positum solutionem maximi mini-
mi ve continebit. Vocabo autem hoc incrementum va-
riationem differentialem formulae $\int Z dx$, quae oritur [?]
intelligenda est, si singuli valores ipsius $y$ particulis in-
finite paruis $\delta y$ iisque arbitrariis augeantur. Tum ve-
ro hanc variationem per omnes valores ipsius $x$, a ter-
mino $x=0$ vsque ad terminum $x=a$, extendi debere
perspicuum est, pro cuius completa determinatione ob-
seruandum est, eam ita sumi oportere, vt posito $x=0$
ea euanescat. Hinc igitur sequentia problemata ope
huius methodi resoluamus; circa quae tenendum est,
litteras $p$, $q$, $r$, $s$ etc. rationem differentialium binarum
variabilium $x$ et $y$ ita inuoluere, vt sit
$p=\frac{dy}{dx}$; $q=\frac{dp}{dx}$; $r=\frac{dq}{dx}$; $s=\frac{dr}{dx}$ etc.
Problema I.
Si Z sit functio quaecunque variabilium $x$ et $y$,
quantitatumque earum differentialia inuoluentium, $p$, $q$,
$r$, $s$ etc. ita vt eius differentiale sit huiusmodi:
$dZ = M dx + N dy + P dp + Q dq + R dr + S ds$ etc.
inuenire variationem differentialem formulae integralis
$\int Z dx$ a termino $x=0$ vsque ad $x=a$ extensam.
Solutio.
Quaeri ergo debet $\delta \int Z dx$; et cum sit $\delta \int Z dx$
$= \int \delta Z dx$, habebimus statim, ob $\delta x = 0$,
$\delta Z = N\delta y + P\delta p + Q\delta q + R\delta r + S\delta s$ etc.
Est

MAXIMORVM ET MINIMORVM. 117
Est vero, sumto differentiali $dx$ constante,
$\delta p = \frac{\delta dy}{dx} = \frac{d\delta y}{dx}$
$\delta q = \frac{\delta dp}{dx} = \frac{d\delta p}{dx} = \frac{dd\delta y}{dx^2}$
$\delta r = \frac{\delta dq}{dx} = \frac{d\delta q}{dx} = \frac{d^3\delta y}{dx^3}$
$\delta s = \frac{\delta dr}{dx} = \frac{d\delta r}{dx} = \frac{d^4\delta y}{dx^4}$;
vnde obtinebimus:
$\delta Z = N\delta y + P\frac{d\delta y}{dx} + Q\frac{dd\delta y}{dx^2} + R\frac{d^3\delta y}{dx^3} + S\frac{d^4\delta y}{dx^4}$ etc.
Iam pro integratione formulae $\int \delta Z dx$, per partes in-
stituenda, vidimus esse
$\int N\delta y\, dx = \int \delta y\, dx.\, N$
$\int P d\delta y = P\delta y - \int \delta y\, dP$
$\int Q\frac{dd\delta y}{dx} = Q\frac{d\delta y}{dx} - \frac{\delta y}{dx}dQ + \int \frac{\delta y}{dx}ddQ$
$\int R\frac{d^3\delta y}{dx^2} = R\frac{dd\delta y}{dx^2} - \frac{d\delta y}{dx^2}dR + \frac{\delta y}{dx^2}ddR - \int \frac{\delta y}{dx^2}d^3R$
$\int S\frac{d^4\delta y}{dx^3} = S\frac{d^3\delta y}{dx^3} - \frac{dd\delta y}{dx^3}dS + \frac{d\delta y}{dx^3}ddS - \frac{\delta y}{dx^3}d^3S - \int \frac{\delta y}{dx^3}d^4S$
etc.
Ex his ergo colligitur variatio differentialis quaesita:
$\delta \int Z dx = \int \delta y\, dx (N - \frac{dP}{dx} + \frac{ddQ}{dx^2} - \frac{d^3R}{dx^3} + \frac{d^4S}{dx^4} - \text{etc.})$
$+ \delta y (P - \frac{dQ}{dx} + \frac{ddR}{dx^2} - \frac{d^3S}{dx^3} + \text{etc.})$
$+ \frac{d\delta y}{dx}(Q - \frac{dR}{dx} + \frac{ddS}{dx^2} - \text{etc.})$
$+ \frac{dd\delta y}{dx^2}(R - \frac{dS}{dx} + \text{etc.})$
$+ \frac{d^3\delta y}{dx^3}(S - \text{etc.})$
vbi pars prima integralis a termino $x=0$ vsque ad
$x=a$ extendi debet, quae ergo omnes variationes in-
termedias complectitur: in reliquis autem partibus ab-
solutis statim ponere licet $x=a$, et $\delta y$ denotabit in-
cremen-
P 3

items.quote: Hinc igitur sequentia problemata ope huius methodi resoluamus
items.english: Hence let us therefore solve the following problems by means of this method.

items.quote: Si Z sit functio quaecunque variabilium $x$ et $y$, quantitatumque earum differentialia inuoluentium, $p$, $q$, $r$, $s$ etc. ita vt eius differentiale sit huiusmodi: $dZ = M dx + N dy + P dp + Q dq + R dr + S ds$ etc. inuenire variationem differentialem formulae integralis $\int Z dx$ a termino $x=0$ vsque ad $x=a$ extensam.
items.english: If Z is any function of the variables x and y and of the quantities p, q, r, s etc. involving their differentials, so that its differential is dZ = M dx + N dy + P dp + Q dq + R dr + S ds etc., find the differential variation of the integral formula ∫Z dx extended from x=0 to x=a.
